decisions.statement: `grantee scope` (11.08.01 D-15) is GRANT-SIDE ONLY. It states who this instrument runs to; it is not a value space in which an owner authors refusals. Buyer blocks stay outside the grammar, evaluated at request time. 11.04.02 D-09, DT-07, the domain CX's CX-16 and CX-18, rejected pair R-08 and 11.04.03's fold all stand unchanged — their premise is corrected, their behaviour is not.
decisions.rationaleRecorded: 11.08.01 DT-15 argues the axis end to end from DELIVERY failure — an agency licence that does not run to the brand is worthless paper — and never once from refusal. The axis exists to make a grant land, not to express a 'no'. Written into DT-15's own Outcome cell and into D-18's Context.

containmentHoleClosure.hole: 11.08.01 D-04 makes an unset axis `unspecified` and fails containment. If grantee is an axis of every scope point, a policy that never names a grantee — which is every policy, since no grantee control is rendered to an owner — contains no request at all, and auto-approve is dead catalogue-wide. Neither 11.08.01 nor 11.04.02 said which reading applied.
containmentHoleClosure.closedBy: A typing rule, not a default value. D-18 states that policies do not carry the grantee axis at all, and that containment is evaluated over the EIGHT policy-bearing axes only (media, data use, territory, term, exclusivity, usage, scale, extent of use). A policy is a predicate over eight axes, NOT a scope point with a ninth axis left unset — so D-04 never fires on it. No permissive default was introduced anywhere; D-04's fail-closed behaviour on the axes an object actually carries is untouched.
